        return c.execute(q, a).fetchall()
    finally:
        c.close()


class Run:
    def __init__(self, topic, out):
        self.topic, self.out = topic, Path(out) / topic
        self.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.log = self.out / "log.jsonl"
        self.log.write_text("")
        self.scratch = SCRATCH / topic
        self.scratch.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.db = self.scratch / "topic.db"
        shutil.copyfile(CANON, self.db)
        self.sess = f"session_2026-11-12-stress-{topic}"
        self.n = 0
        self.index = []

    # one logged step -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def step(self, tag, expect, argv, db=None, cwd=REPO, timeout=300, stdin=None):
        db = Path(db or self.db)
        assert db.resolve() != CANON.resolve()
        self.n += 1
        tag = f"{self.topic}.{self.n:03d}.{tag}"
        s0, b = sha(CANON), counts(db)
        env = dict(os.environ, GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH=str(db))
        t0 = time.time()
        try:
            p = subprocess.run(argv, cwd=cwd, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout, input=stdin)
            rc, so, se = p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
            rc, so, se = "TIMEOUT", "", "timeout"
        except Exception as e:  # noqa
            rc, so, se = "SCRIPT-ERROR", "", traceback.format_exc()
        dt = round(time.time() - t0, 2)
        try:
            a = counts(db)
        except Exception as e:  # noqa
            a = {"__unreadable__": str(e)}
        ch = {t: [b.get(t), a.get(t)] for t in set(b) | set(a) if b.get(t) != a.get(t)}
        s1 = sha(CANON)
        rec = dict(tag=tag, expect=expect, argv=argv, cwd=str(cwd), db=str(db), rc=rc, seconds=dt, stdout=so, stderr=se,
                   changed=ch, canonical_moved=(s0 != s1), canonical_sha256=s1, at=time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()))
        with open(self.log, "a") as f:
            f.write(json.dumps(rec, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
        first = (so.strip().splitlines() or [""])[0][:140] if so else (se.strip().splitlines() or [""])[-1][:140]
        self.index.append((tag, rc, dt, len(ch), expect, first))
        print(f"{tag} rc={rc} {dt}s changed={len(ch)}", flush=True)
        return rc, so, se

    def note(self, tag, expect, result):
        """Log a read-only fact taken directly from the DB (no subprocess)."""
        self.n += 1
        tag = f"{self.topic}.{self.n:03d}.{tag}"
        rec = dict(tag=tag, expect=expect, argv=["<direct read-only query>"], rc=0, stdout=json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, default=str),
                   stderr="", changed={}, at=time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()))
        with open(self.log, "a") as f:
            f.write(json.dumps(rec, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
        self.index.append((tag, 0, 0, 0, expect, json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)[:140]))
        return result

    def dbpy(self, tag, expect, *args, **kw):
        return self.step(tag, expect, [PY, "-I", "scripts/db.py", *args], **kw)

    def sql(self, tag, expect, q, a=()):
        try:
            r = rows(self.db, q, a)
            return self.note(tag, expect, {"sql": q, "params": list(a), "rows": r[:200], "nrows": len(r)})
        except Exception as e:  # noqa
            return self.note(tag, expect, {"sql": q, "error": repr(e)})

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Deterministic stress script: run the pipeline base -> render, then backward, cold-entry, lateral
and adversarial, for three unrelated topics, on SCRATCH copies, logging every command.

    python3 -I stress_run.py [--topics acoustics,reach,thermal] [--out DIR]

Nothing here judges. Every step records an EXPECTATION (written before the run), the command, rc,
full stdout/stderr, and the row-count change on the scratch DB, to <out>/<topic>/log.jsonl. A later
audit (Fable) reads the logs. A step that raises inside this script is logged as SCRIPT-ERROR and the
run continues. The canonical DB is never written (sha256 recorded around every step); steps that write
into a source tree (emit_data_migration, migrate_db) run in a local clone.

def sha(p):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(p).read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def ro(db):
    return sqlite3.connect(f"file:{db}?mode=ro", uri=True)


def counts(db):
    c = ro(db)
    try:
        return {t: c.execute(f'select count(*) from "{t}"').fetchone()[0]
                for (t,) in c.execute("select name from sqlite_master where type='table' and name not like 'sqlite_%'")}
    finally:
        c.close()


def rows(db, q, a=()):
    c = ro(db)
    try:
        return c.execute(q, a).fetchall()
    finally:
        c.close()


class Run:
    def __init__(self, topic, out):
        self.topic, self.out = topic, Path(out) / topic
        self.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.log = self.out / "log.jsonl"
        self.log.write_text("")
        self.scratch = SCRATCH / topic
        self.scratch.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.db = self.scratch / "topic.db"
        shutil.copyfile(CANON, self.db)
        self.sess = f"session_2026-11-12-stress-{topic}"
        self.n = 0
        self.index = []

    # one logged step -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def step(self, tag, expect, argv, db=None, cwd=REPO, timeout=300, stdin=None):
        db = Path(db or self.db)
        assert db.resolve() != CANON.resolve()
        self.n += 1
        tag = f"{self.topic}.{self.n:03d}.{tag}"
        s0, b = sha(CANON), counts(db)
        env = dict(os.environ, GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH=str(db))
        t0 = time.time()
        try:
            p = subprocess.run(argv, cwd=cwd, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout, input=stdin)
            rc, so, se = p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
            rc, so, se = "TIMEOUT", "", "timeout"
        except Exception as e:  # noqa
            rc, so, se = "SCRIPT-ERROR", "", traceback.format_exc()
        dt = round(time.time() - t0, 2)
        try:
            a = counts(db)
        except Exception as e:  # noqa
            a = {"__unreadable__": str(e)}
        ch = {t: [b.get(t), a.get(t)] for t in set(b) | set(a) if b.get(t) != a.get(t)}
        s1 = sha(CANON)
        rec = dict(tag=tag, expect=expect, argv=argv, cwd=str(cwd), db=str(db), rc=rc, seconds=dt, stdout=so, stderr=se,
                   changed=ch, canonical_moved=(s0 != s1), canonical_sha256=s1, at=time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()))
        with open(self.log, "a") as f:
            f.write(json.dumps(rec, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
        first = (so.strip().splitlines() or [""])[0][:140] if so else (se.strip().splitlines() or [""])[-1][:140]
        self.index.append((tag, rc, dt, len(ch), expect, first))
        print(f"{tag} rc={rc} {dt}s changed={len(ch)}", flush=True)
        return rc, so, se

    def note(self, tag, expect, result):
        """Log a read-only fact taken directly from the DB (no subprocess)."""
        self.n += 1
        tag = f"{self.topic}.{self.n:03d}.{tag}"
        rec = dict(tag=tag, expect=expect, argv=["<direct read-only query>"], rc=0, stdout=json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, default=str),
                   stderr="", changed={}, at=time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()))
        with open(self.log, "a") as f:
            f.write(json.dumps(rec, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
        self.index.append((tag, 0, 0, 0, expect, json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)[:140]))
        return result

    def dbpy(self, tag, expect, *args, **kw):
        return self.step(tag, expect, [PY, "-I", "scripts/db.py", *args], **kw)

    def sql(self, tag, expect, q, a=()):
        try:
            r = rows(self.db, q, a)
            return self.note(tag, expect, {"sql": q, "params": list(a), "rows": r[:200], "nrows": len(r)})
        except Exception as e:  # noqa
            return self.note(tag, expect, {"sql": q, "error": repr(e)})

def sha(p):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(p).read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def ro(db):
    return sqlite3.connect(f"file:{db}?mode=ro", uri=True)


def counts(db):
    c = ro(db)
    try:
        return {t: c.execute(f'select count(*) from "{t}"').fetchone()[0]
                for (t,) in c.execute("select name from sqlite_master where type='table' and name not like 'sqlite_%'")}
    finally:
        c.close()


def rows(db, q, a=()):
    c = ro(db)
    try:
        return c.execute(q, a).fetchall()
    finally:
        c.close()


class Run:
    def __init__(self, topic, out):
        self.topic, self.out = topic, Path(out) / topic
        self.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.log = self.out / "log.jsonl"
        self.log.write_text("")
        self.scratch = SCRATCH / topic
        self.scratch.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.db = self.scratch / "topic.db"
        shutil.copyfile(CANON, self.db)
        self.sess = f"session_2026-11-12-stress-{topic}"
        self.n = 0
        self.index = []

    # one logged step -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def step(self, tag, expect, argv, db=None, cwd=REPO, timeout=300, stdin=None):
        db = Path(db or self.db)
        assert db.resolve() != CANON.resolve()
        self.n += 1
        tag = f"{self.topic}.{self.n:03d}.{tag}"
        s0, b = sha(CANON), counts(db)
        env = dict(os.environ, GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH=str(db))
        t0 = time.time()
        try:
            p = subprocess.run(argv, cwd=cwd, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout, input=stdin)
            rc, so, se = p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
            rc, so, se = "TIMEOUT", "", "timeout"
        except Exception as e:  # noqa
            rc, so, se = "SCRIPT-ERROR", "", traceback.format_exc()
        dt = round(time.time() - t0, 2)
        try:
            a = counts(db)
        except Exception as e:  # noqa
            a = {"__unreadable__": str(e)}
        ch = {t: [b.get(t), a.get(t)] for t in set(b) | set(a) if b.get(t) != a.get(t)}
        s1 = sha(CANON)
        rec = dict(tag=tag, expect=expect, argv=argv, cwd=str(cwd), db=str(db), rc=rc, seconds=dt, stdout=so, stderr=se,
                   changed=ch, canonical_moved=(s0 != s1), canonical_sha256=s1, at=time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()))
        with open(self.log, "a") as f:
            f.write(json.dumps(rec, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
        first = (so.strip().splitlines() or [""])[0][:140] if so else (se.strip().splitlines() or [""])[-1][:140]
        self.index.append((tag, rc, dt, len(ch), expect, first))
        print(f"{tag} rc={rc} {dt}s changed={len(ch)}", flush=True)
        return rc, so, se

    def note(self, tag, expect, result):
        """Log a read-only fact taken directly from the DB (no subprocess)."""
        self.n += 1
        tag = f"{self.topic}.{self.n:03d}.{tag}"
        rec = dict(tag=tag, expect=expect, argv=["<direct read-only query>"], rc=0, stdout=json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, default=str),
                   stderr="", changed={}, at=time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()))
        with open(self.log, "a") as f:
            f.write(json.dumps(rec, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
        self.index.append((tag, 0, 0, 0, expect, json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)[:140]))
        return result

    def dbpy(self, tag, expect, *args, **kw):
        return self.step(tag, expect, [PY, "-I", "scripts/db.py", *args], **kw)

    def sql(self, tag, expect, q, a=()):
        try:
            r = rows(self.db, q, a)
            return self.note(tag, expect, {"sql": q, "params": list(a), "rows": r[:200], "nrows": len(r)})
        except Exception as e:  # noqa

+

+def writepath_replay(R, T):
+    clone = R.scratch / "clone"
+    if not clone.exists():
+        R.step("writepath.clone", "local clone for write-path replay", ["git", "clone", "--quiet", str(REPO), str(clone)])
+    canon_copy = R.scratch / "canonical-copy.db"
+    shutil.copyfile(CANON, canon_copy)
+    out_sql = R.scratch / "batch.sql"
+    R.step("writepath.emit-batch-sql", "capture the scratch DB's delta as SQL", [PY, "-I", "scripts/research/emit_batch_sql.py", "--scratch", str(R.db), "--canonical", str(canon_copy), "--out", str(out_sql)])
+    if out_sql.exists() and out_sql.stat().st_size:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Per-script probe of the live text guards. Reads only; prints JSON.
Usage: python3 -I lang_probe.py '<json {label: string}>'
Loads the repo's functions by path and applies them to the given strings:
  - research/retrieval_log.normalise_quote   (quote verification)
  - dbcore.normalise_quote_text              (the dbcore copy)
  - db._name_tokens / db._VALUE_BEARING_NAME (term-name screens)
Reports normalised form, token set, whether a value-bearing screen fires, and
any set of DIFFERENT input strings that normalise to the SAME text (a collision).
"""
import importlib.util, json, sys
from pathlib import Path
R = Path("/home/user/guidebook/scripts")
sys.path.insert(0, str(R))

def load(name, rel):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, R / rel)
    m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(m)
    return m

out = {"errors": {}}
mods = {}
for n, rel in (("rl", "research/retrieval_log.py"), ("dbcore", "dbcore.py"), ("dbmod", "db.py")):
    try:
        mods[n] = load(n, rel)
    except BaseException as e:  # noqa
        out["errors"][n] = repr(e)
strings = json.loads(sys.argv[1])
res = {}
for label, s in strings.items():
    r = {"input": s}
    for fn, key in ((("rl", "normalise_quote"), "rl.normalise_quote"), (("dbcore", "normalise_quote_text"), "dbcore.normalise_quote_text")):
        try:
            r[key] = getattr(mods[fn[0]], fn[1])(s)
        except BaseException as e:  # noqa
            r[key] = f"ERROR {e!r}"
    try:
        r["db._name_tokens"] = sorted(mods["dbmod"]._name_tokens(s))
    except BaseException as e:  # noqa
        r["db._name_tokens"] = f"ERROR {e!r}"
    try:
        r["db._VALUE_BEARING_NAME_fires"] = bool(mods["dbmod"]._VALUE_BEARING_NAME.search(s))
    except BaseException as e:  # noqa
        r["db._VALUE_BEARING_NAME_fires"] = f"ERROR {e!r}"
    res[label] = r
out["per_string"] = res
for key in ("rl.normalise_quote", "dbcore.normalise_quote_text"):
    g = {}
    for label, r in res.items():
        v = r.get(key)
        if isinstance(v, str) and not v.startswith("ERROR"):
            g.setdefault(v, []).append(label)
    out["collisions_" + key] = [v for v in g.values() if len(v) > 1]
# strings whose name-token set is empty (the near-match refusal examines nothing)
out["empty_name_token_sets"] = [l for l, r in res.items() if r["db._name_tokens"] == []]
print(json.dumps(out, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1))
EOF

input.message:
Two jobs, one pass. Owner goal: the stress-test output gives you more review/audit surface so your recommendations and plan are as good as possible; and the independent Fable antagonist's confirmation found residual inaccuracies in your amended files.

PART A — fix the residual inaccuracies. /home/user/guidebook/scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/audit/fa-confirmation.md (verdict: accurate enough to build on; 46 accurate / 22 inaccurate / 1 unverifiable; 5 material, 17 minor). Re-run each inaccuracy's evidence, then correct the audit files: especially (1) IMP-12's 'delete gap_mining' vs IMP-05's caller-sweep condition (unswept callers: registry gap_mining_audit, test_run_pipeline_refusals.py, graph/topology.py, gap-driven-mining skill); (2) fa-corrections-for-suite.md §4 incomplete (C-03, C-07, C-10, C-14, C-15, C-19, C-20 etc. — rebuild it from the full 28-row table); (3) AT-53 not restated against IMP-07's ruled-gate change; (4) the order the ledger does NOT state for IMP-40 before T-3 (PS:4934, PS:4938) — say it is your sequencing; (5) the claim that the repo already seeds 'the other defects' (one has no seeded test); plus the 17 minors (parameter 12 fails C10 for one source not four; AT-76 'For: IMP-16' remnant; REQ-019 wording; line-22 stale sentence; typed 'three governance files' vs four; brief: 'four rounds' vs five steps, 'three permitted searches' vs a fourth, document 2's queue-vs-decisions pointer, document 3's missing 9 x MOB run, document 4's wave scope, three warrant labels, the PS:4761 paraphrase). Update resolution records accordingly.

PART B — audit the stress-test results. Location: /home/user/guidebook/scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/stress/ — results/<topic>/log.jsonl (authoritative, complete), results/<topic>/scenarios.tsv, results/<topic>/determinations/*.json (engine reports), results/run-console.txt; the script is stress_run.py, the language probe lang_probe.py, the protocol STRESS-BRIEF.md. Nine unrelated topics (acoustics, reach, thermal, luminance, circadian, flash, grabbar, cost, method) plus a 'crosstopic' replay; passes: forward base->render, backward, cold entry, lateral (script/number-format probes, jurisdiction and language-code vocabulary probes), adversarial inputs, determinism, write-path replay in a clone. The script is deterministic and mechanical; it does not judge. YOU judge. It is itself a surface to audit: some refusals may be caused by the script's own arguments rather than the pipeline — separate script-induced behaviour from pipeline behaviour, and say where the script is too weak to have tested what it claims. Do the following:
 1. Classify every notable behaviour (as-designed / defect / silent no-op / vacuous pass / refusal-correct / refusal-wrong / doc-contradiction), per topic and across topics; identify what is the SAME across topics (systemic) versus topic-specific. Derive counts by command.
 2. Compare to your audit's predictions: what was confirmed, what the stress tests contradict, and what you MISSED. Look especially at: the crosstopic rebuild failure (rc 1) and what it implies for parallel research batches and id allocation; the second assess run on the same DB (rc 1) and determinism claims; vocabulary behaviour for sub-national jurisdictions and language codes (CA-ON, DE-NW, XX, zh-Hant, ZZ); script-level text-guard collisions per script (Devanagari, Thai, Hebrew, kana, Hangul, Arabic, full-width digits, Indian digit grouping, currency formats); the dynamic parameter-definition route (observe -> add-term -> add-parameter) and what happens to the read-once ledger when the parameter list grows (scan_debt, v_scan_ledger); cold-entry refusals at each stage and their messages (do they say what to do next?); engine behaviour for a defined-but-unevidenced parameter (parameter 7, and any newly defined one) across lenses; render (owner_browser_build output, walkability, v_best_practice for cells without determinations); the write-path replay (emit_batch_sql counts, emit_data_migration, migrate_db --rebuild, rebuilt-vs-scratch differences).
 3. Revise your improvement programme, acceptance tests, preconditions, ordering and owner-decision list in light of this: new defects -> new IMPs/ATs/ODs with the same justification fields; contradicted predictions -> corrected; reorder if the stress tests show a dependency you missed. Record each change in fa-corrections-for-suite.md (as a new section 'Stress-test deltas') so the downstream suite can absorb it.
 4. Retention. +        fresh = R.scratch / f"v-{v}.db"
+        shutil.copyfile(CANON, fresh)
+        argv = [PY, "-I", "scripts/db.py", v, *args] + (["--dry-run"] if has_dry else [])
+        R.step(f"verb.{v}", f"{v}: mechanically-built required args from real DB values; {'--dry-run' if has_dry else 'real run on a fresh copy'}", argv, db=fresh)
+    R.note("sweep.coverage", "every db.py verb invoked", {"verbs": len(verbs), "invoked": len([x for x in R.index if '.verb.' in x[0]])})
+    finish_(R)
+
+
+def part_tools(out):
+    R = Run("tools", out)
+    before = subprocess.run(["git", "status", "--porcelain", "--", ".", ":!scratchpad", ":!transcripts"], cwd=REPO, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
+    audits = sorted(p for p in (REPO / "scripts/audit").glob("*.py"))
+    for p in audits:
+        R.step(f"audit.{p.stem}", f"{p.name} run bare on a scratch DB: examines something, or says what it needs", [PY, "-I", str(p.relative_to(REPO))], timeout=300)
+    for p in sorted((REPO / "scripts").glob("validate_*.py")) + [REPO / "scripts/doctrine_recheck.py"]:
+        R.step(f"validate.{p.stem}", f"{p.name} bare", [PY, "-I", str(p.relative_to(REPO))], timeout=300)
+    for p in sorted((REPO / "scripts/research").glob("*.py")):
+        R.step(f"research.{p.stem}.help", f"{p.name} --help", [PY, "-I", str(p.relative_to(REPO)), "-h"])
+    R.step("research.mining_screen.compare", "citation-mining screens compared over deposited references", [PY, "-I", "scripts/research/mining_screen.py", "--all", "--compare"])
+    R.step("registry.list", "registry + quarantine, runs nothing", [PY, "-I", "scripts/run_checks.py", "--list"])
+    for b in ("syntax", "structure", "data", "db_integrity", "schema", "governance", "attestation", "research", "render", "tests"):
+        R.step(f"registry.battery.{b}", f"battery {b} on the scratch DB", [PY, "-I", "scripts/run_checks.py", "--battery", b], timeout=900)
+    R.step("registry.selftest", "selftest (where a rename fails)", [PY, "-I", "scripts/run_checks.py", "--selftest"], timeout=600)
+    R.step("registry.changed-from-main", "diff-scoped gate against origin/main, explained", [PY, "-I", "scripts/run_checks.py", "--changed-from", "origin/main", "--explain"], timeout=900)
+    after = subprocess.run(["git", "status", "--porcelain", "--", ".", ":!scratchpad", ":!transcripts"], cwd=REPO, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
+    R.note("tools.repo-tree-changed-by-tools", "no tool wrote into the repository tree outside scratchpad/transcripts", {"before": before, "after": after, "changed": before != after})
+    finish_(R)
+
+
+def part_chain(out):
+    """A real held source through the verbs round 1 never reached, in one persistent scratch DB, ids re-read between steps."""
+    R = Run("chain", out)
+    S = R.sess
+    ref = "REF-00139"
+    sc = rows(R.db, "select file_sha256 from source_scans where ref_id=? and text_scope='full' limit 1", (ref,))
+    ex = rows(R.db, "select extraction_id,parameter_id,claim_text,claimed_value,claimed_unit,claim_type from source_value_extractions where ref_id=? order by extraction_id limit 1", (ref,))
+    R.note("chain.anchor", "a real held source with a full-text scan and extractions", {"ref": ref, "scan_sha": sc, "extraction": ex})
+    if sc and ex:
+        eid, pid, claim, val, unit, ctype = ex[0]
+        R.dbpy("chain.record-scan-real", "a real full reading names bytes the retrieval log holds", "record-scan", "--ref-id", ref, "--mode", "catalogue", "--text-scope", "full",
+               "--file-sha256", sc[0][0], "--method", "full-read", "--session", S)
+        words = re.findall(r"[A-Za-z]{4,}", claim)
+        if len(words) >= 2:
+            R.dbpy("chain.observe-term-real", "a phrase observed verbatim from the held text", "observe-term", "--ref-id", ref, "--surface-form", " ".join(words[:2]), "--language", "en",
+                   "--locator", "STRESS-FIXTURE locator", "--context-quote", claim[:200], "--session", S)
+        R.dbpy("chain.add-extraction-second-row", "a dissenting/second row for an already extracted figure under another lens (D-0168 contest)", "add-extraction", "--ref-id", ref, "--parameter-id", str(pid),
+               "--claim-type", ctype or "numerical", *(["--claimed-value", str(val)] if val is not None else []), *(["--claimed-unit", unit] if unit else []), "--claim-text", claim[:300],
+               "--extraction-method", "full-read", "--identity", "DEAF", "--figure-role", "claim", "--relation", "none", "--session", S)
+    c = ctx(R.db)
+    for v in ("is-mined", "log-mining", "unmined", "add-locator", "update-locator", "link-source-slug", "link-admission", "unlink-admission", "add-population-match", "amend-population-match",
+              "add-case-study", "add-economics-entry", "add-supersession-check", "supersede-source", "correct-source", "amend-source", "amend-extraction", "relate-extraction",
+              "derive-extraction", "raise-follow-up", "resolve-follow-up", "add-conflict", "update-conflict", "conflicts", "connections", "update-connection", "delete-connection",
+              "add-code-lead", "update-code-lead", "add-alias", "amend-term", "rename-term", "decline-parameter", "revoke-declination", "annotate-parameter", "set-parameter-direction",
+              "merge-parameter", "raise-determination-gate", "resolve-determination-gate", "retire-specification", "record-adversarial-pass", "dispose-adversarial-finding",
+              "close-adversarial-pass", "add-gap-mining", "close-gap", "amend-gap", "update-gap-addressability", "gaps", "next-id"):
+        c = ctx(R.db)
+        args, has_dry = build_args(v, c, S)
+        R.step(f"chain.verb.{v}", f"{v} in sequence on the persistent chain DB with ids re-read from it", [PY, "-I", "scripts/db.py", v, *args])
+    # determination after the chain, and the replay
+    fresh = R.scratch / "chain-assess.db"
+    shutil.copyfile(R.db, fresh)
+    if ex:
+        R.step("chain.assess-after-chain", "determine the anchor's parameter after the chain's additions", [PY, "-I", "scripts/assess/assess_cell.py", "--db", str(fresh), "--emit-sql", str(R.scratch / "chain.sql"),
+               "--parameter-id", str(ex[0][1]), "--slug", "accessible-circulation-geometry", "--identity", "MOB", "--session", S, "--stamp", "2026-11-12 00:00:00",
+               "--report-json", str(R.out / "chain-assess.json")], db=fresh)
+    out_sql = R.scratch / "batch.sql"
+    R.step("chain.emit-batch-sql", "capture everything the chain wrote", [PY, "-I", "scripts/research/emit_batch_sql.py", "--scratch", str(R.db), "--canonical", str(CANON), "--out", str(out_sql)])
+    finish_(R)
+
+
+def finish_(R):
+    from stress_run import finish
+    finish(R)
+
+
+def main():
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    ap.add_argument("--out", default=str(HERE / "results2"))
+    ap.add_argument("--parts", default="sweep,chain,tools")
+    a = ap.parse_args()
+    s0 = sha(CANON)
+    for part in a.parts.split(","):
+        {"sweep": part_sweep, "chain": part_chain, "tools": part_tools}[part](a.out)
+    print("canonical sha256 before/after:", s0, sha(CANON), "UNCHANGED" if s0 == sha(CANON) else "!!! MOVED !!!")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Stress script, round 3: DEPTH. Fixes the round-1/2 script faults the audit named (hs-stress-audit.md §4, W-1..W-11) and
runs its seven further scenarios on a REAL held source (REF-00139): read to the end, evidenced cells across lenses with the
gates, the write path with a determination compared by content, parallel batches at capture, the fidelity guards through
the writers, the parameter life cycle, and backward/re-entry in rows. Plus every registry battery run correctly.

    python3 -I stress_run3.py [--out DIR] [--parts real,guards,batches,lifecycle,reentry,batteries,probes]

Scratch copies only; the canonical DB is never written (hash recorded around every step). It does not judge.
Faults it corrects: the observed phrase is a CONTIGUOUS bigram of the quote; every extraction carries a locator;
batteries run as `--battery <name> --all`; no placeholder arguments on the steps that matter; engine runs share ONE
database per scenario so the gates and views see the determination.
"""
import argparse, json, re, shutil, sqlite3, subprocess, sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from stress_run import Run, rows, sha, CANON, REPO, PY, SCRATCH, HERE, counts  # noqa: E402
from stress_run2 import ctx, build_args, finish_  # noqa: E402

REF = "REF-00139"
SLUG = "accessible-circulation-geometry"


def anchor(db):
    sc = rows(db, "select file_sha256 from source_scans where ref_id=? and text_scope='full' limit 1", (REF,))
    ex = rows(db, "select extraction_id,parameter_id,claim_text,claimed_value,claimed_unit,claim_type,source_section from source_value_extractions where ref_id=? order by extraction_id limit 1", (REF,))
    return (sc[0][0] if sc else None), (ex[0] if ex else None)


def bigram(claim):
    m = re.search(r"([A-Za-z]{4,}) ([A-Za-z]{4,})", claim)
    return m.group(0) if m else None


def add_ext(R, tag, ex, lens, value=None, unit=None, expect="a correctly cited second row under another lens is accepted", db=None, extra=()):
    eid, pid, claim, val, u, ctype, sect = ex

## Owner statement 2026-11-12 (fifth) — the overall code is efficient, centralized and clean

Made in the session that audited the pipeline (`session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit`), recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Quoted verbatim:

> "ensure the overall code is efficient and centralized and clean"

**What this records.** A standing requirement on the code as a whole: efficient (no avoidable cost in time or in repeated work), centralized (one home for each rule, vocabulary, function and fact, so a change is made once), and clean (no dead, duplicated or contradictory apparatus). It extends and does not replace the 2026-10-12 and 2026-11-06 statements on minimising code and the rule-5 and rule-8 doctrine of one home per fact.

**What it does not decide.** Which duplications to remove first, whether a large module is split, and what counts as "efficient" for each tool are open and belong to the audit's improvement programme. A cleanup is a change to code and is held to the same rules as any: behaviour-preserving unless a defect is being fixed, callers swept (rule 4), tooling apart from research rows (rule 10), and proven by a test that could go red. [ASSUMPTION: "overall code" is read as the scripts, schemas, checks, skills and hooks, not the guidebook's prose or data.]

CONDITION: any session adding, moving, merging or deleting code, or asked whether a piece of code is redundant, duplicated or in the wrong place.
ACTION: (1) Prefer one home per rule, vocabulary or function, and point to it rather than copy it. (2) Delete dead and duplicated code on evidence. (3) Measure efficiency before changing it. (4) Preserve behaviour under a refactor and prove it with a before-and-after comparison. (5) Treat the [ASSUMPTION] mark above as unratified.
DATE: 2026-11-12 — owner statement, quoted above.
EOF
TS=$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M'); git add references/project-standards.md && git commit -q -m "governance: record owner statement on efficient, centralized, clean code [$TS]

input.message:
New live owner statement (2026-11-12), recorded verbatim at references/project-standards.md 'Owner statement 2026-11-12 (fifth)': "ensure the overall code is efficient and centralized and clean". Treat as REQ-101 and carry it through JOB 1 and JOB 2 of my last message (it extends the 2026-10-12 / 2026-11-06 minimise-code statements and rules 5 and 8).

Add to your audit and the remediation workplan a CODE QUALITY track, evidence first, derived not typed:
 - CENTRALIZED: measure duplication and multiple homes with commands — same function in several files (e.g. the normalise_quote copies and dbcore.normalise_quote_text, the name screens, vocabularies maintained beside their column CHECK (argparse choices= vs dbcore.schema_choices/check_values), constants/lists/globs/thresholds that restate a checked value, the hand-written 'N today' counts in governance/check-registry.yaml and prose, parallel lists of tables/stages/verbs, copies of the same SQL across scripts, two homes for one fact in the schema), and the module structure of the largest files (scripts/db.py, assess_cell.py, dbcore.py, run_checks.py, retrieval_log.py): what is a coherent unit and what is accretion; whether splitting the db.py monolith is warranted or a risk not worth taking, with the evidence.
 - CLEAN: dead and orphaned code by evidence (unreferenced functions via AST/caller sweep, unregistered checks, uncalled scripts, tables/columns/verbs nothing reads or writes, skills presupposing deleted structures, stale comments that contradict code, commented-out blocks, workplan/ scripts and tools that are superseded), contradictions between prose and code, inconsistent conventions (argument naming, session-id forms, error/exit-code conventions, output formats), and the gaps the stress tests showed (silent no-ops; delete-connection on a missing id exits 0; --battery usage).
 - EFFICIENT: measure before proposing — startup/import cost of db.py, per-verb and per-check wall time (the stress logs record seconds per step: use them), the slowest registry batteries (tests took ~79 s in round 3), repeated DB opens or full-table scans in hot paths, anything O(n^2) over the tables at their current and plausibly 100x size, checks that re-read what they did not change. Say which costs matter for the owner's goal (dynamic runs on demand) and which do not.
 For each finding: the evidence command, the one home it should have, what is deleted/merged/moved, the caller sweep (rule 4), the behaviour-preservation proof, and the task id in the workplan. Behaviour-preserving refactors must be proven with a before/after comparison — use the retained stress scripts (stress_run.py, stress_run2.py, stress_run3.py) as characterization harnesses: run them on the tree before and after the change and diff the logs (argv, rc, stdout/stderr, row deltas); note which fields vary by time/path and must be normalised. Order the code-quality tasks so that deletions and centralizations that REDUCE code come early (and make later tasks smaller), refactors of the hot, high-risk files come last or are explicitly declined with reasons, and nothing here mixes with research rows (rule 10). Rule 8 stays: nothing added without naming what reads it; the measure `git diff --shortstat origin/main -- scripts schemas .github skills ':!scripts/migrations'` is reported per task.

Short answer: yes, `/run-pipeline` runs today, and it will still run after the workplan. What changes is whether you can trust what it produces and how far it reaches.

**Today.** It runs, but the results can't be trusted. On a scratch copy, parameter 3 × Deaf people came back `provisional`, built from 122 extractions that are all tagged for mobility. No determination is live, so the blocking specification gates examine only retired history.

**After Wave 0**, which is 18 tasks needing no owner decision, it gives more honest output:
- Wrong claimed numbers are refused.
- Refusals say what to do next.
- Checks report whether they examined anything.
- Stage-entry and cell-status queries exist.

**After the critical path**, a first determination is for the group it names. That path runs T-014 → T-008 → T-016 → T-017 → T-018 → T-019 → {T-104, T-102, T-106} → T-110. Two links are not Sonnet's to start: T-018 needs a design from Fable, and T-102 needs your answer on OD-14 plus an Opus-class session.

**What will still stop it until you answer:**

content.text:
Yes, with a triage first and a bound on the loop. Not every failure needs Opus.

**Triage each pilot failure into one of four classes:**

1. **Executor error.** Sonnet misread or skipped a step the file stated clearly. This is a Sonnet problem, not a plan problem. Re-run it with a corrected prompt, and don't change the plan.
2. **Task-file defect.** A wrong or missing flag, a path that doesn't exist, an expected output that doesn't match, a missing precondition. Fix the file mechanically. A planner can do it, and Opus isn't needed.
3. **Judgment problem.** The task as designed doesn't achieve its stated objective, two tasks conflict, a fix breaks something else, or the change needs a design decision the file doesn't settle. This goes to an Opus-class model. The project floor, "Opus-class or above", includes Fable.
4. **Owner-gated.** The failure turns on doctrine. It goes to the decision register, not to a model.

**Nulls count as failures.** A pass where the check examined nothing proves nothing, and the pilots are told to report it that way. A pilot that reports "green" without saying what the check examined gets re-run.

**Fold the fix back, and re-prove it.** For classes 2 and 3, the corrected task is re-piloted in a fresh clone by a Sonnet executor, using only the task file. That's a re-execution of the same steps, not another round of argument, so it fits your "stop looping" instruction. The cycle is bounded: one correction pass per task. If it still fails after that, the task is marked blocked with the reason, and it goes to you.

**Who does the judgment.** Fable wrote the plan and has the context, which is why I'd use it for class 3. The drawback is that a planner correcting its own plan can anchor. For any class 3 fix that changes a task's design, not just its wording, I'd have a different Opus-class instance review the change.

I'll apply this to the three pilots as they report.

Three Sonnet executors each took ONE Wave-0 task in a scratch clone, following only the task file: reports + patches in /home/user/guidebook/scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/pilot/{T-006,T-008,T-010}-report.md and .patch (committed). Read all three reports and patches in full. The change worked in all three (red before / green after); the task files had defects. Triage them (class 1 executor error: ignore; 2 mechanical task-file defect: fix; 3 judgment problem: decide; 4 owner-gated: register) and correct the plan.

KNOWN DEFECTS from the pilots:
A. Systemic (probably in all 55 files — scan EVERY task file for each pattern and fix by command): (1) the integration base: in a clone, origin/main is 106 commits behind the branch carrying the workplan, so 'git switch -c … origin/main', the shortstat command and the default preflight base all diff the whole workplan — state the precondition 'this workplan PR is merged to main; until then base on the workplan branch (name it) and gate with --changed-from HEAD / preflight --base HEAD~1', and make the commands base-agnostic where possible; (2) gate order vs commit order (a diff-scoped gate needs the change committed first) and the gate step running preflight.sh AND run_checks.py on the same diff (twice; CLAUDE.md says run once); (3) '/session-open' and 'git switch -c task/…' conflicting with a clone/pilot — say when each applies; (4) the sweep commands print ~50-200 mostly irrelevant lines (generated workplan/pipeline-state-graph files, old workplans, ledger) so the stop condition 'a caller this file does not mention' is unsatisfiable — give each sweep an explicit exclusion list/filter and an expected-hits list; (5) 'read its EXAMINED: line for every check' cannot be followed: passing checks print no EXAMINED line in preflight/--explain — name the command that prints each check's subject, per check; (6) hard-coded ids in tests/evidence (TERM-041, TERM-075) against the rule not to type what the DB can derive, and test-id collisions (P01-P09 exist; the executor used AP1-AP5; N10/N11) — specify id allocation by derivation; (7) write-verb evidence commands need the inline GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH reminder beside the command; (8) §8 'add nothing the file does not name' vs §5 sweep-found fixes — reconcile: a sweep-found caller fix is IN scope and must be listed in the pull request; (9) a stale 'declined term' trap in 'still works' probes (TERM-089 'ramp' is DECLINED — exclude declined terms).
B. T-006: D1-D9 in its report (name update_connection_status; which test file hosts N10/N11; scratch() copy for the positive case; a worked add-connection command; name the check to read).
C. T-010: the caller sweep missed real callers — scripts/tests/test_scan_contract.py (V03 promotes FREE[10] = TERM-017 'universal design', a methodology term, so it regresses under the new rule) and a stale comment in scripts/research/research_batch_dod.py — add them; say what the refusal must tell the reader to do (the executor wrote 'file it as a GAP; do not hand-write SQL' because no verb corrects a term's domain: that is itself a dead end under REQ-103 — decide: add the verb, or state the route); the quantity-domain set was implemented as a new constant dbcore.NON_QUANTITY_DOMAINS — judge it against rule 8/one-home (should it be derived from a column, e.g. the quantity-kind column of IMP-30b/OD-24, rather than a list?).
D. T-008 — CLASS 3, needs your judgment: (1) section 4 item 2 as written CREATES A DEAD END: a spelled-out claimed_value (Finnish 'viisi prosenttia', Dutch 'vijf', German cardinals) has no numeral, and the verbatim-exempt route is refused whenever the text verifies, so such values become unfilable — this is open GAP-056 (REF-01017, extraction 80); the executor implemented the rule as written and flagged it. Decide the design that satisfies both 'a claimed number is checked as a number' and 'no dead ends' (e.g. a typed spelled-number reading per language set as data not code, or a sanctioned exemption path with a recorded reason) and say whether any part is an OWNER DECISION (it touches non-English handling: REQ-097 D3); (2) the new check would REFUSE two stored rows (extraction 30 Dutch 'vijf' claimed 5, which the old check passed only because 5 is a substring of 50; extraction 80) — decide the treatment of existing rows (history stands; amend-extraction route; or flag) and put it in the task; (3) which claim types 'state a quantity' (executor hard-coded numerical and range) — derive from the column CHECK; (4) number forms: 'AS 1428.1:2021' and table cell '800 750' falsely refused by a naive ratio reading, '1 in 12' needed, 'plain 12 accepted under 1:12' residual, ambiguous '1,200' handled by admitting both readings (so 1.2 passes against '1,200 mm') — decide the intended behaviour and write it into the task with tests; (5) amend-extraction is not a reader of _require_verbatim (readers: add-extraction, derive-extraction) — fix the task; (6) _verbatim_norm: say delete; (7) prose callers: GAP-056 text in data migrations and sessions/ needs a pointer note (data migrations are immutable: say where the note goes); (8) the evidence command reimplements the old logic and cannot show the AFTER — give a recipe that runs the real writer function.
Also record the pilots' outcome in REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md as a short section (what was piloted, results, what changed in the plan because of it) and add a 'pilot status' line to each of T-006, T-008, T-010 once corrected. For every other task file: apply fixes A1-A9 by command and list in the workplan index which tasks were pilot-tested (3) and which were not, so the executor knows the untested ones carry more risk. Same rules: derive counts, Canadian English, plan only (no script/schema/governance/DB edits), DB read-only with sha256 before/after. Reply with the list of changes, the class-3 decisions you made with reasons, new owner decisions (if any), and the tasks still unpiloted.

> lol just translate these into numbers/units as applicable. you can have an untranslated column for provenance if you want"

## Owner statement 2026-11-12 (ninth) — everything non-English is translated, probably at synthesis, or wherever it is needed

Made in the session that audited the pipeline (`session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit`), directly after the eighth statement (spelled-out numbers translated into numerals and units), recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Quoted verbatim:

> "probably at synthesis or whatever we need to actually translate everything"

**What this records.** The text the pipeline holds in other languages (quotations, terms, clauses, titles) is to be translated, all of it, so that it can be compared and discussed together. The owner's view of where is "probably at synthesis", and "or whatever we need": the stage is not fixed in advance, and translation is available wherever a stage needs it. Read with the eighth statement, a number is translated at extraction because the number check needs a numeral there; the rest is translated when and where it is needed, probably at synthesis.

**What it does not decide.** Which stage owns translation by default, who or what translates (a person, a model, a tool) and at what class, how a translation is marked so it is never taken for the source's own words, whether a translation is reviewed, and which language is translated into (the language of a page: OD-02). It narrows OD-02 on one point only: that quotations may be translated. It does not relax the rule that a model's wording is never presented as a source's term (OR-17, E1), or the 2026-11-06 statements that English is not the pivot that decides which concepts exist (the sixth and eighth statements of that date). [ASSUMPTION: "translate everything" is read as a standing capability of the pipeline, held apart from the source text and pointing at it, not as the replacement of the source text by its translation.]

CONDITION: any session translating, or deciding where translation happens, or presenting a translated quotation, term or clause.
ACTION: (1) Treat translation as a capability to be called at the stage that needs it, not as a step fixed in one stage. (2) Keep the untranslated text and attach the translation to it by pointer, marked as a translation with its translator. (3) Never present a translation as the source's own wording. (4) Leave the default stage, the translator's class and the target language to the audit's programme and the owner. (5) Treat the [ASSUMPTION] mark above as unratified.
DATE: 2026-11-12 — owner statement, quoted above.
EOF
TS=$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M'); git add references/project-standards.md && git commit -q -m "governance: record owner statement that everything non-English is translated [$TS]

Probably at synthesis or wherever needed; the capability is stage-agnostic.
Recorded verbatim per rule 0; mechanism and defaults left to the programme.

I've recorded your statement on translation and pushed it. It's with the plan's author.

I read it this way, and it's marked unratified in the entry:
- **Translate everything.** All non-English text the pipeline holds gets translated, so it can be compared and discussed together. That means quotes, terms, clauses and titles.

- A typed home for translations, with a verb callable from any stage. It has to share one design with the as-written provenance column from T-008.

- A test that translates a quote by data alone and leaves the original unchanged.

## Owner statement 2026-11-12 (tenth) — a rule that synthesis translates is not necessarily hard-coding

Made in the session that audited the pipeline (`session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit`), directly after the ninth statement (everything non-English is translated, probably at synthesis), recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Quoted verbatim:

> "we can set a rule for synthesis to translate, which isn't hardcoding necessarily"

**What this records.** Synthesis may be given a rule to translate, and a rule of that kind is not, of itself, a hard-coded behaviour in the sense of the seventh statement. It is a gloss on the line between the two: a behaviour held once, as a stated rule that can be read and changed in one place, is permitted; a behaviour fixed as a literal or a branch scattered through code is not.

**What it does not decide.** Where the rule is held (the pipeline contract, the check registry, a configuration table), how it is read, and whether the owner or the implementer may change it. The "necessarily" leaves cases open: a rule can still be hard-coding if it is buried in code or restated in several places. It does not make translation exclusive to synthesis (ninth statement: wherever it is needed). [ASSUMPTION: the sentence is read as setting synthesis as the default stage for translation by a rule held in one place that other stages can override or call, not as fixing translation to synthesis alone.]

CONDITION: any session placing translation, or any other default behaviour, in a stage, or judging whether a stated rule is hard-coding.
ACTION: (1) Hold a default behaviour, including "synthesis translates", as a rule in one stated place and read it from there. (2) Do not scatter it as a literal or a name-branch in code. (3) Keep the capability callable from other stages. (4) Treat the [ASSUMPTION] mark above as unratified.
DATE: 2026-11-12 — owner statement, quoted above.
EOF

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Derive the remediation plan's dependency batches from the task files. Reads only; writes REMEDIATION-PLAN.md.

    python3 -I scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/build_batches.py

Nothing here is typed in: ids, titles, kinds, executors, owner decisions and hard dependencies come from each
task file's own text (section 1 table; section 2 bullets 'Tasks that must be merged' and 'Owner decisions').
A dependency written 'none (after T-nnn if both are open ...)' is SOFT: an ordering hint, not a gate.
Batch = 1 + the longest chain of hard dependencies. Within a batch, tasks that touch the same file are one
SERIAL LANE (merge in the lane's order); different lanes may be worked in parallel.
"""
import re, subprocess, datetime, collections
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("/home/user/guidebook")
W = ROOT / "workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline"
OUT = W / "REMEDIATION-PLAN.md"
TASKS = sorted((W / "tasks").glob("T-[0-9]*-*.md"))


def section(text, n):
    m = re.search(rf"^## {n}\. .*?$(.*?)(?=^## \d+\. |\Z)", text, re.S | re.M)
    return m.group(1) if m else ""


def cell(text, label):
    m = re.search(rf"^\| {label} \| (.*?) \|\s*$", text, re.M)
    return m.group(1).strip() if m else ""


def bullet(sec2, label):
    m = re.search(rf"^- \*\*{label}[^*]*\*\*(.*?)(?=^- \*\*|\Z)", sec2, re.S | re.M)
    return m.group(1).strip() if m else ""


tasks = {}
for f in TASKS:
    t = f.read_text()
    tid = re.match(r"# (T-\d+)", t).group(1)
    title = re.sub(r"^# T-\d+\s+", "", t.splitlines()[0]).strip()
    s2, s4 = section(t, 2), section(t, 4)
    dep_txt = bullet(s2, "Tasks that must be merged")
    dep_txt = dep_txt.split("Check by running")[0]
    soft = set()
    if dep_txt.lower().lstrip().startswith("none ("):
        soft = set(re.findall(r"T-\d+", dep_txt))
        hard = set()
    elif dep_txt.lower().lstrip().startswith("none"):
        hard = set()
    else:
        hard = set(re.findall(r"T-\d+", dep_txt))
    hard.discard(tid)
    od_txt = bullet(s2, "Owner decisions")
    ods = set() if od_txt.lower().startswith("none") else set(re.findall(r"OD-\d+", od_txt))
    paths = sorted(set(re.findall(r"`((?:scripts|schemas|governance|skills|\.claude|\.github)/[A-Za-z0-9_./\-]+\.[a-z]+)`", s4)))
    paths = [p for p in paths if "/migrations/" not in p]
    tasks[tid] = dict(
        id=tid, file=f.name, title=title, wave=cell(t, "Wave"), kind="RESEARCH" if "RESEARCH" in cell(t, "Kind") else "TOOLING",
        sonnet="NOT FOR SONNET" not in cell(t, "Executor"), hard=hard, soft=soft, ods=ods, paths=paths,
        piloted=bool(re.search(r"\*\*Pilot status\.\*\*\s*(Piloted|Partly|Executed)", t)))

# --- batches: longest chain of hard dependencies
memo, stack = {}, set()


def depth(t):
    if t in memo:
        return memo[t]
    if t in stack:
        raise SystemExit(f"CYCLE through {t}")
    stack.add(t)
    d = 1 + max([depth(x) for x in tasks[t]["hard"] if x in tasks] or [0])
    stack.discard(t)
    memo[t] = d
    return d


missing = sorted({d for t in tasks.values() for d in t["hard"] if d not in tasks})
for t in tasks:
    tasks[t]["batch"] = depth(t)
nb = max(t["batch"] for t in tasks.values())

# --- status
def status(t):
    if not t["sonnet"]:
        return "NOT FOR SONNET"
    if t["ods"]:
        return "OWNER: " + ",".join(sorted(t["ods"], key=lambda x: int(x[3:])))
    return "READY"


# a task is 'reachable by Sonnet' if it and every hard ancestor is READY
def anc(t, seen=None):
    seen = seen if seen is not None else set()
    for d in tasks[t]["hard"]:
        if d in tasks and d not in seen:
            seen.add(d)
            anc(d, seen)
    return seen


for tid, t in tasks.items():
    t["status"] = status(t)
    blockers = [a for a in anc(tid) if status(tasks[a]) != "READY"]
    t["reach"] = "yes" if t["status"] == "READY" and not blockers else ("after " + ", ".join(sorted(blockers, key=lambda x: int(x[2:]))) if t["status"] == "READY" else "no")

# --- serial lanes inside a batch: connected components over shared paths and soft deps
def lanes(ids):
    parent = {i: i for i in ids}

    def find(x):
        while parent[x] != x:
            parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]
            x = parent[x]
        return x

    def union(a, b):
        parent[find(a)] = find(b)

    for a in ids:
        for b in ids:
            if a < b and (set(tasks[a]["paths"]) & set(tasks[b]["paths"]) or b in tasks[a]["soft"] or a in tasks[b]["soft"]):
                union(a, b)
    comp = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for i in ids:
        comp[find(i)].append(i)
    key = lambda i: (tasks[i]["kind"] == "RESEARCH", int(i[2:]))
    return sorted((sorted(v, key=key) for v in comp.values()), key=lambda v: key(v[0]))


# --- owner-decision queue
od_blocks = collections.defaultdict(list)
for tid, t in tasks.items():
    for o in t["ods"]:
        od_blocks[o].append(tid)

# --- critical path (longest hard chain)
def chain(t):
    best = []
    for d in tasks[t]["hard"]:
        if d in tasks:
            c = chain(d)
            if len(c) > len(best):
                best = c
    return best + [t]


crit = max((chain(t) for t in tasks), key=len)

sha = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC")
L = []
A = L.append
A("# Remediation plan, in batches by dependency\n")
A(f"_Generated {now} from the {len(tasks)} task files at commit {sha} by `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/build_batches.py`. "
  "Nothing below is typed in: re-run the generator (`python3 -I scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/build_batches.py`) after any task file changes, and trust the generator over this text (CLAUDE.md rule 7a)._\n")
A("**What this is.** The entry document for a Sonnet executor. `REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md` is the index (why, owner decision register, Definition of Done); `tasks/T-<id>-*.md` is the one self-contained file per task; this file says **in what order, in what groups, and where to stop.** "
  "Evidence base: `01-handshake-ledger.md` and the audit in `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/audit/`.\n")
A("## 1. How to execute\n")
A("1. **Merge this workplan first.** Every task file sets `$BASE` to `origin/main` once the workplan is on it, and to the workplan branch before that.")
A("2. **Take one batch at a time, in order.** A batch is the set of tasks whose hard dependencies all lie in earlier batches. Do not start batch *n* until every READY task of batch *n-1* is merged and its after-test is green on `$BASE`.")
A("3. **Inside a batch, work lanes in parallel and tasks in a lane serially.** A lane is a set of tasks that touch the same file (or that a task file says to sequence). Merge a lane's tasks in the order listed.")
A("4. **One task, one pull request, one executor, one task file.** Run the task's red test before, the same test after, the gate once (`scripts/preflight.sh --base \"$BASE\" --explain`), and the adversarial pass once before opening the pull request. Rule 9: open the pull request last, then unsubscribe.")
A("5. **Stop at a status that is not READY.** `OWNER: OD-nn` means the owner's answer (in the form the register gives) must be in `references/project-standards.md` first. `NOT FOR SONNET` means an Opus-class session or the Fable agent does it. Neither is an invitation to improvise.")
A("6. **Tooling merges before the research it unlocks (rule 10).** A research task never shares a pull request with tooling, and its row writes go only through the write path of CLAUDE.md §4.")
A("7. **The first execution of an unpiloted task is its pilot.** List any defect found in its task file in the pull request.\n")
A("## 2. The batches at a glance\n")
A("| Batch | Tasks | READY | OWNER-blocked | NOT FOR SONNET | Tooling / research | Lanes |")
A("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
for b in range(1, nb + 1):
    ids = [t for t in tasks if tasks[t]["batch"] == b]
    c = collections.Counter(tasks[t]["status"].split(":")[0] for t in ids)
    A(f"| {b} | {len(ids)} | {c['READY']} | {c['OWNER']} | {c['NOT FOR SONNET']} | {sum(tasks[t]['kind']=='TOOLING' for t in ids)} / {sum(tasks[t]['kind']=='RESEARCH' for t in ids)} | {len(lanes(ids))} |")
A("\nCounts are derived; the commands that check them: `ls workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/tasks/T-[0-9]*-*.md | wc -l`, and the generator's own output.\n")
A(f"**Longest dependency chain ({len(crit)} tasks):** " + " → ".join(f"{t} ({tasks[t]['status']})" for t in crit) + ".\n")
if missing:
    A(f"**Dependencies naming a task with no file (fix the task file):** {', '.join(missing)}\n")

for b in range(1, nb + 1):
    ids = [t for t in tasks if tasks[t]["batch"] == b]
    A(f"## Batch {b}\n")
    if b == 1:
        A("**Entry:** the workplan is on the integration base. No task is a prerequisite.\n")
    else:
        prev = sorted({d for t in ids for d in tasks[t]["hard"]}, key=lambda x: int(x[2:]))
        A("**Entry:** merged and green on `$BASE`: " + ", ".join(prev) + ".\n")
    A("| Task | Title | Wave | Kind | Status | Reachable by Sonnet now | Hard deps | Pilot |")
    A("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for t in sorted(ids, key=lambda x: int(x[2:])):
        x = tasks[t]
        A(f"| [{t}](tasks/{x['file']}) | {x['title'][:90]} | {x['wave']} | {x['kind']} | {x['status']} | {x['reach']} | {', '.join(sorted(x['hard'], key=lambda y: int(y[2:]))) or '—'} | {'piloted' if x['piloted'] else 'not piloted'} |")
    A("\n**Lanes** (parallel across, serial within; the shared file is the reason):\n")
    for i, lane in enumerate(lanes(ids), 1):
        shared = sorted(set.intersection(*[set(tasks[t]["paths"]) for t in lane])) if len(lane) > 1 else []
        why = f" — share `{shared[0]}`" if shared else (" — sequenced by a soft dependency or a chain of shared files" if len(lane) > 1 else "")
        A(f"- Lane {b}.{i}: " + " → ".join(lane) + why)
    stops = sorted({tasks[t]['status'] for t in ids if tasks[t]['status'] != 'READY'})
    A("\n**Exit:** every READY task above is merged and its section 6 after-test is green on `$BASE`; `scripts/preflight.sh --base \"$BASE\" --explain` is green on `$BASE`." +
      (f" **Stops in this batch:** {'; '.join(stops)}." if stops else "") + "\n")

A("## Owner decision queue (what each answer releases)\n")
A("Answer forms and options are in the register in `REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md` (grep `^### OD-`). An answer binds only once the ledger quotes it (`references/project-standards.md`).\n")
A("| Decision | Releases | In batches |")
A("|---|---|---|")
for o in sorted(od_blocks, key=lambda x: int(x[3:])):
    A(f"| {o} | {', '.join(sorted(od_blocks[o], key=lambda x: int(x[2:])))} | {', '.join(str(b) for b in sorted({tasks[t]['batch'] for t in od_blocks[o]}))} |")
inreg = set(re.findall(r"^### (OD-\d+)", (W / "REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md").read_text(), re.M))
A(f"\nDecisions in the register that no task file lists as a precondition: {', '.join(sorted(inreg - set(od_blocks), key=lambda x: int(x[3:]))) or 'none'}.\n")
A("## NOT FOR SONNET\n")
A("| Task | Title | Batch | Owner decisions |")
A("|---|---|---|---|")
for t in sorted((t for t in tasks if not tasks[t]["sonnet"]), key=lambda x: int(x[2:])):
    x = tasks[t]
    A(f"| [{t}](tasks/{x['file']}) | {x['title'][:80]} | {x['batch']} | {', '.join(sorted(x['ods'])) or '—'} |")
A("\nEach file says who does it. Everything that depends on one of these waits for it (the 'Reachable by Sonnet now' column names the blockers).\n")
A("## Where the pilots stand\n")
A("`grep -L \"Not piloted\" workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/tasks/T-*.md` lists the tasks a pilot has touched. Results, defects found and what changed in the plan are in section 12 of `REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md` and in `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/pilot/`.\n")
OUT.write_text("\n".join(L))
print("tasks", len(tasks), "batches", nb, "missing deps", missing, "crit", len(crit))
for b in range(1, nb + 1):
    ids = [t for t in tasks if tasks[t]["batch"] == b]
    print(b, len(ids), collections.Counter(tasks[t]["status"].split(":")[0] for t in ids))

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

content.text:
The plan should take the pipeline from "runs one cell forward on a scratch copy, with results you can't trust" to the pipeline you described. Each point below ties to your own statements, and each has a Definition-of-Done command that is red today.

**1. Determinations you can trust (the most important one).**
- A determination is for the group it names.
- Today the engine ignores the lens: parameter 3 × Deaf people is built from figures all tagged for mobility, and no gate catches it.
- Also: wrong numbers are refused (the claimed-number check), the gates examine live determinations and not retired history, and the mobility split you ruled gets executed.

**2. Any direction, any stage, dynamic.**
- Entry and re-entry are representable in rows, with typed gaps, and any cell's status can be asked at any stage.
- No stage pair is left without a path, and a lost path is detected.
- Render is the exception. It stays blocked until you answer the render decisions (OD-02, OD-08, OD-12).

**3. A robust base for languages, jurisdictions and terms.**
- Adding a language, jurisdiction or vocabulary term is data, not a code change.
- Scope is recorded in a table (today 0 of 70 language–jurisdiction rows have a scope status).
- The quote and name guards work outside Latin script.
- Concepts don't depend on English strings, and everything non-English can be translated, with the original kept and the translation attached by pointer.

**4. Read once, miss nothing.** Parameters are defined dynamically, and the debt a new parameter creates for already-read sources is visible and dischargeable. How it's discharged (re-read or retained text) waits on your decision, OD-23.

**5. Abstract parameters, and synthesis that finds relations.** Commonality across clauses and jurisdictions is representable, and equivalence, adjacency and similarity can be found on demand. That needs OD-24 (parameter granularity) and OD-07, OD-19 and OD-25 (synthesis).

**6. Clean, centralized, flexible, with no dead ends.**
- Helpers have one home, and defaults are stated rules held once, not scattered literals.
- Every refusal says what to do next.
- Tables nothing can write, and rows that can't be corrected or ended, are removed or opened.

**What it does not accomplish by itself:**
- It executes nothing. It is a plan, and PR #217 contains no code change.
- Three of its 58 tasks have been tried by an executor, and the rest are unpiloted.
- A lens-correct first determination also needs your OD-14 answer and a design from Fable (T-018), and the 28+ other owner decisions stand until you answer them.

The proof that it worked is the Definition-of-Done commands turning green on `main`, each run by someone who didn't write the change.

Fable could resolve **20 of the 29 standing decisions**, and **9** would still need you. That is my classification, made by reading each entry's own "why it is the owner's" line against your three criteria. Recount the total with `grep -c "^### OD-" REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md`, which gives 29 because OD-16 was withdrawn.

**The 20 Fable can resolve.** For each, the criteria point to a determinate answer.
- **Design and definition, low residual risk (18):**
  - OD-02 page language
  - OD-03 concepts with no English name
  - OD-05 out-of-scope evidence from mining
  - OD-06 which stage assigns lenses
  - OD-07 what a synthesis row is
  - OD-08 what an absent cell means
  - OD-10 what `provisional` means
  - OD-11 gap-register owner
  - OD-12 how render prose is produced
  - OD-18 what "all directions" covers
  - OD-20 the owner's edits
  - OD-21 questions about a published cell
  - OD-22 rounding direction
  - OD-24 parameter granularity
  - OD-25 synthesis relations
  - OD-26 interim stage-pair gate
  - OD-29 retire-in-place for link rows
  - OD-30 who translates
- **Consequential, so I'd still have you ratify (2):** OD-01 (jurisdiction in a determination) and OD-14 (carrying the rows written under `MOB`). The criteria point to an answer, but these shape the book's central claim and its treatment of a population.

**The 9 it cannot resolve by those criteria:**
- **OD-04, OD-28:** only you can say what your own earlier answer covered or what you said.
- **OD-13, OD-17:** retiring one of your rules, and ratifying the contract, are your acts.
- **OD-15, OD-23:** these turn on licensing, such as the WHO position or holding and showing a standard's text. That is an external legal fact.
- **OD-09, OD-27:** these set how much the project may run unattended and how fast research goes, which is trajectory and control.
- **OD-19:** weighing one group's harm against another's is the ethical core and your CRPD posture. The criteria name ethical approaches but don't settle it.

Of the decisions that release the most work, Fable could resolve OD-24, OD-14, and OD-02, OD-08 and OD-12 (render). It could not resolve OD-04 or OD-23.

**Conditions I'd attach:**
1. **You record the delegation.** CLAUDE.md §8 names these subjects as yours. Your own precedents are the 2026-09-11 and 2026-10-14 delegations in the ledger, so it should be a recorded delegation naming the set.
2. **Provenance.** Each answer is recorded as "Fable's resolution under delegation", with the criterion that decided it. It is never recorded as your word, and it is reversible.
3. **A priority between the criteria.** Rigour, legibility and coverage can pull apart. For example, a legible render sentence can overstate a thin ○ cell. Tell me whether your numbering is the order.
4. **Interpretations stay interpretations.** OD-06, OD-18, OD-20 and OD-29 read your words. Fable can choose a defensible reading but can't say what you meant.
5. **An independent check on the doctrine-heavy ones.** A different Opus-class instance should check OD-01, OD-02, OD-12 and OD-14 before they are relied on.

input.body:
## What this changes

Documents only; no schema, script, migration, check or data change (`data/guidebook.db` sha256 unchanged throughout). Follow-on to #217.

- **`references/project-standards.md`** (append-only; zero existing lines removed):
  - the owner's delegation, recorded verbatim ("I guess opus can do it"), with the three criteria, the set of twenty, the nine reserved decisions and the conditions on how a delegated resolution is held;
  - 18 delegated resolutions, each labelled as an Opus-class resolution under delegation and not the owner's words, with the deciding criterion and a reversal condition;
  - corrections after the independent review (OD-01, OD-02, OD-12), the withdrawal of OD-14, and the gate convention (`OD-nn STATUS:` / `OD-nn CHECK:`).
- **`workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/`**:
  - `DELEGATED-RESOLUTIONS.md` (the reasoning, per decision) and `DELEGATED-RESOLUTIONS-REVIEW.md` (the independent review of OD-01/02/12/14);
  - five new task files (T-050, T-051, T-052, T-053, T-113) and 27 updated task files, each keeping the 11-section structure;
  - `REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md` (register, Definition of Done) updated, `REMEDIATION-PLAN.md` regenerated (63 tasks, 7 batches, no missing dependency, no cycle), and `FOLD-LOG.md` (every file changed and why).

## What needs the owner

- **OD-10 and OD-14 are referred back whole.** OD-10: the owner has given "provisional" two meanings (2026-09-09 and 2026-10-30), and every option overrides one. OD-14: the independent reviewer found the delegated resolution retired a standing owner ruling (the 2026-08-25 fan-out) on a reason the owner never gave; it was withdrawn, and a narrower sound version is described for the owner to accept or not.
- **Nine decisions stay reserved**: OD-04, OD-09, OD-13, OD-15, OD-17, OD-19, OD-23, OD-27, OD-28.
- **Any delegated resolution is reversible by the owner at any time.** OD-12 is the most contestable (it reaches OW-1b's "mixed" option without the owner's review); OD-02 and OD-01 are moderate.
- Five new owner questions are in `FOLD-LOG.md` (PQ-1 to PQ-5), not yet in the register.
- The numbering of the criteria is assumed to be their priority order (unratified).

## Known limits

- `build_batches.py` reads only the "Owner decisions" bullet, not the new gate, so a task whose decisions are all delegated shows READY; each executor's own gate command is what stops the work. Fixing it is a script change, excluded here.
- None of the new or edited task files has been piloted.
- The raw D-27 grep (`OD-nn:` count) is superseded by the STATUS/CHECK convention: OD-14 still contains the token but its status is CLOSED.

## Checks

Diff-scoped gate (`scripts/preflight.sh`): PASS, 24 green, 4 nothing-in-scope, 2 advisory failures (`skill_vocabulary_audit`, `retired_vocabulary`), both red on untouched `main`.

definition.description:
Withdraw a task suggestion you queued earlier with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion has gone stale: the issue was fixed in this session (by you or the user), it turned out not to be a problem after all, or you have queued a better-scoped replacement — in that case queue the replacement with spawn_task first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only a suggestion the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn. If they already started, dismissed or edited it, the result says so and nothing changes; that answer is final, so don't retry or re-flag it.

Read the result before you start the task anew or do it here: after "Not withdrawn", don't start it anew, and do it here only if the user asks for that in chat.

reason.description: Optional short note on why the suggestion is no longer needed, e.g. "fixed in this session" or "superseded by task_ab12cd34". It doesn't change the outcome.

task_id.description: The task_id from the spawn_task result that queued the suggestion (of the form task_1a2b3c4d).

definition.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
definition.description:
Suggest a separate task for something you noticed that is outside the scope of your current work.

Call this when you come across something that deserves fixing but doesn't belong in this change — dead code, stale docs, a missing test, a confirmed TODO, a bug or security issue spotted in passing. Don't use it for trivial fixes you can make inline, for anything the user asked you to do, for vague code-smell impressions or unverified hunches, or to split off parts of your own task. The call only queues a suggestion and returns; carry on with your current work.

The user sees a "Suggested task" card in the Claude desktop app with your title and tldr, can open the full prompt, and with one click starts it as a new session — on their machine in their local clone of this repository (optionally a fresh worktree of it), or in the cloud — sends it to this session, or dismisses it. A new session starts from your prompt alone, on a checkout that may not have this session's changes, so the prompt has to stand alone: what to change and why, the files involved by repository-relative path, and any context from this conversation it depends on. Absolute paths and other state of this environment may not exist there. If the find involves a secret or credential, say where it is rather than copying the value, since the prompt is stored and displayed.

The result carries a task_id; if the suggestion later becomes moot, withdraw it with dismiss_task.

prompt.description: The opening message of the new session: the goal, the files involved by repository-relative path, the context it needs from this conversation, and what done looks like. The user can read it in full before starting; markdown is fine. Keep it to what the task needs (hard limit 32000 characters) — the new session can read the code itself.

title.description: The card's heading and the new session's title: a short imperative phrase starting with a verb, under 60 characters, that makes sense on its own — e.g. "Fix stale README badge", "Remove dead config option".

tldr.description: One or two plain sentences on what the task would do and why it is worth doing. Shown on the card under the title; it is what the user reads when deciding whether to start it, so no file paths or code.
